title: Weight tenancy leasing and KV preload protocol for predictable cold-start latency
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated tenant fleets still experience multi-second cold starts when model weights are staged and KV caches are empty. That spikes tail latency and violates throughput guarantees for some enterprise customers during sudden traffic bursts.

Goal: Implement a lightweight leasing protocol for weight tenancy (a short-term lease that guarantees weight residency on a host) combined with a KV preload coordinator so that: (1) essential model shards are resident on at least N nodes per shard group; (2) KV caches are proactively seeded with recent prefixes for high-QPS tenants; and (3) eviction/lease-renewal is policy-driven to balance residency costs vs. cold-start risk.

Constraints: must be compatible with Dedicated fleet autoscaling and existing warm-pool primitives, preserve tenant isolation and billing accounting, and avoid increasing steady-state memory pressure beyond configurable limits. The mechanism should operate within the runtime (no new RPC hop to control plane per request) and expose telemetry for eviction churn, lease hit-rate, and preload success rates.
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff — aligned with infra and runtime teams. Agreed on three coordinator roles: lease-manager (per-fleet), preload-scheduler, and local-residency-agent.

2026-03-02: Prototype — implemented lease-manager with optimistic leases stored in etcd; local-residency-agent honors leases and pins weights into GPU/CPU residency; initial benchmark shows median cold-start improvement from 1.6s -> 420ms for small model shards.

2026-03-05: Trade-off discussion — two approaches evaluated: (A) strict pinned residency with higher memory footprint; (B) soft-lease with probabilistic eviction. Decided to ship soft-lease by default with configurable reserved memory percent and an opt-in strict residency flag for high-tier customers.

2026-03-09: KV preload plan — preload-scheduler will use recent traffic traces and tenant traffic-weighted sampling to seed KV caches via a background bulk-warm RPC. Prototype warms top-1k prefixes per tenant per shard group; observed 65% hit-rate improvement on replay traffic.
2026-03-11: Security & billing — added audit hooks so residency leases are tagged with tenant id and billed as memory-reservation hours. SRE asked for limits to prevent noisy-tenant eviction storms.

2026-03-12: PR opened — https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4498 (lease-manager + preloader). Initial code review feedback requested additional unit tests and stronger invariants around lease renewal windows.
2026-03-13: Integration tests running on staging; night-run scheduled to validate interactions with autoscaler and Dedicated burst policy.
acceptance_criteria: Tail p95 cold-start latency for dedicated tenants during a controlled ramp <= 500ms for baseline model families configured with tenancy leases
Lease hit-rate metrics exist and are > 85% for tenants enrolled in the residency program in staging traffic replay
KV preload success rate > 70% for seeded prefixes within 60s of enrollment
No unbounded memory leaks; residency memory usage respects configured reserved percent and triggers backpressure when exceeded
End-to-end test validating autoscaler respects residency leases and does not evict leased nodes prematurely
Docs updated: Confluence design doc and Console UI flags for enabling strict residency and configuring preload budgets
